lines.text: Everyday clothing is what most people wear for daily activities — work, errands, and casual outings. The basics include a T-shirt, which is the most universal garment, worn by people of all ages. Jeans are equally popular — durable, comfortable, and suitable for almost any informal occasion. A hoodie or sweatshirt provides warmth on cool days, while a jacket or coat is essential in colder weather. For the upper body, options range from a simple blouse or shirt to a cardigan or pullover. Trousers come in many styles: chinos, leggings, joggers, and cargo pants each serve different purposes. Shorts are common in warm weather, and a skirt or dress offers alternatives for those who prefer them. Underwear — including briefs, boxers, socks, and undershirts — forms the invisible foundation of every outfit. Sleepwear like pyjamas and a dressing gown keeps you comfortable at home. Seasonal items like a raincoat, scarf, gloves, and a beanie or woolly hat protect against the elements. Understanding everyday clothing vocabulary helps with shopping, packing for trips, and describing what people are wearing — a skill tested in every language exam.

lines.text: Many clothing items have different names: 'trousers' (UK) vs 'pants' (US), 'jumper' (UK) vs 'sweater' (US), 'trainers' (UK) vs 'sneakers' (US), 'waistcoat' (UK) vs 'vest' (US). In British English, 'pants' means underwear!

lines.text: Many workplaces in English-speaking countries have 'Casual Friday' (or 'Dress-Down Friday'), where employees wear jeans and casual tops instead of business attire. This tradition reflects the importance of comfort in modern work culture.
lines.name: Many workplaces in English-speaking countries have 'Casual Friday' (or 'Dress-Down Friday'), where employees wear jeans and casual tops instead of business attire. This tradition reflects the importance of comfort in modern work culture.

lines.text: English-speaking countries use different size systems: UK sizes differ from US sizes. 'Small (S), Medium (M), Large (L), Extra Large (XL)' are universal. When shopping, always check the label — a UK 12 is a US 8!

lines.text: In countries with changeable weather (UK, Ireland, New Zealand), 'layering' is a key concept. People wear multiple thin layers — T-shirt, shirt, cardigan, jacket — that can be added or removed as the temperature changes throughout the day.
